title: September DMI cut East Africa box rainfall forecast error by 30% in a 2000-2025 test
abstract: We tested whether September Indian Ocean Dipole conditions add forecast information for October-December rain in 5 S-5 N, 35 E-40 E. Each fit used earlier years from 1979. The baseline used September local rain, September Nino 3.4 and a linear trend. Adding September DMI cut mean squared error by 30.1% across 26 forecasts in 2000-2025. RMSE fell from 0.873 to 0.730 mm/day. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for error reduction was 4.0% to 49.4%. The one-year interval was -4.5% to 47.3%, so uncertainty depends on sampling assumptions. Planned checks retained positive point gains. August inputs gave a smaller 12.6% gain; omitting 1997 from training gave 17.2%. This is a retrospective test with revised GPCP, CPC ERSSTv5 and HadISST data. It does not establish real-time skill or physical cause. A small region, short record, source changes and conditional intervals limit the result. The package contains monthly evidence, all forecasts, code, source hashes, draws and independent numerical checks.

display.caption: Observed and predicted October-December rain in the fixed East Africa box. Positive bars show lower annual squared error after September DMI is added. All fits use earlier years only.
